summary: TMA for the pooler weight stream is a reasonable next lever and breaks no rule. But the change also moves BLOCK_K from 128 to 256, and that alone has a measured precedent (the unpooler program at 18.0 us, 3.73 TB/s) close to the hypothesis's own 17.5 us target. So one run cannot credit any gain to TMA. Run it alongside the cp.async BLOCK_K=256 control, which already exists, held, as pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore-control-blockk256.
justification: Mechanism. At m<=32 the pooler is a pure 67.1 MB weight stream. The parent's _bf16_splitk_kernel took 19.5/20.0/19.9/22.7 us of kernel time at m=1/8/16/32. That is 3.44/3.36/3.37/2.96 TB/s against a 14.0-14.1 us floor (4.8 TB/s). Shape times were 20.2/19.9/20.7/22.2 us. That leaves 5-6 us of headroom on four rows, each about 31-38% of its load at equal weight 62, so a real gain would show in the geomean (about +2-3% if 2 us per row). On H200, TMA plus mbarrier bulk copies do cut issue pressure compared with 4 warps issuing 64 cp.async.16 per thread per 32 KB stage. 128 KB in flight per CTA times 128 CTAs is about 16 MB in flight, far above the roughly 5 MB that Little's law needs, so the target can be reached in principle. Shared memory is 160/192 KB, which fits within 227 KB. The [64,256] box is within TMA's 256-element per-dimension limit. Directions are consistent with TASK.md: m=1/8/16 faster, m=128/256 and other layers flat as in-run controls. decode_32 marked flat is defensible. BLOCK_K=256 at BLOCK_M=32 on the unpooler ran 19.8 us of kernel time against the parent's 22.7, so decode_32 may even come out faster, and a TMA effect there is equally unattributable. WEAKEST LINK: the premise that 'every plain-tl.load Triton stream tops out at 3.3 TB/s' is contradicted by LESSONS and by unpooler-full-triton-skinny-m32. That kernel has the same per-CTA geometry this change produces (BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=256, 4 stages, 128 KB in flight, 64 rows x 4096 K) and reached 18.0 us at m=16 (3.73 TB/s) with cp.async. The parent's 3.4 TB/s is explained by its BLOCK_K=128 (64 KB in flight), which the parent's own reviewer flagged. So most of the predicted 20.2 -> 17.5 us is already expected from the bundled BLOCK_K change, and TMA's own increment is the remaining ~0.5 us, below the ~1% Triton reproducibility only marginally. A second weak point is that TMA itself is no guarantee of more than 4 TB/s. cuBLAS's nvjet already uses TMA and moves this same weight at 3.67 TB/s (18.3 us at m=1).
confounders: router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: different layer and kernel, no shared workspace or counters, cold L2 per replay. It cannot move pooler rows. Router rows are only a reproducibility check.
sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: defines the cuBLAS path that pooler m>=128 and all other layers keep. Those rows are flat controls, not an interaction.
router-hilo-at-m8: router-only, now subsumed by the Triton router, with no shared path. Not a confounder.

Not landed but structural: the base is the neutral parent branch (pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore, 1.166x), not master (1.143x). The headline delta against BEST therefore includes the parent's own roughly +2% pooler effect. Read the gain from the per-row kernel us against the parent's 19.5/20.0/19.9/22.7 us, not from the headline.
interference: No landed hypothesis touches the pooler path, its traffic or its numerics, so ab-revert and ab-tune are not warranted. The ambiguity comes from the hypothesis bundling two sub-changes: BLOCK_K 128->256 (doubling bytes in flight) and cp.async->TMA. A gain to about 18 us is exactly what the BLOCK_K change alone predicts from the unpooler precedent, so it cannot be credited to TMA. A flat or lost result is also ambiguous: it could mean TMA does not help, or that TMA's mma.sync operand path costs more than the extra stage bytes buy. Either way the follow-up decision (port TMA to qkv_gate and unpooler, or just use BLOCK_K=256 everywhere) depends on the split. One control resolves both cases: the parent's branch with BLOCK_K=256 and plain tl.load. That code already exists as pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore-control-blockk256. Its hold reason was that a control isolating a sub-change of a neutral parent cannot change a decision, and that no longer applies, because it is now the cp.async arm of this A/B. Re-queue that file rather than minting a duplicate (identical code is never re-run). The slug below is only nominal. One companion is enough. A TMA run at BLOCK_K=128 would be redundant once both 256 runs exist.
rules_flags: No rule problem found. The descriptor is built in prepare() from the weight pointer, shape and strides only, not from data. Device-side TMA with mbarriers, and host descriptors passed as kernel parameters (or, on the old API, a prepare()-filled device descriptor buffer), are graph-capturable. There are no host syncs, and the precision is unchanged (bf16 weight, fp32 accumulate, one bf16 rounding).

On the older experimental API the descriptor lives in a device buffer. It must be created and filled in prepare() and never rebuilt or copied in kernel_fn (a host-to-device copy inside the timed call would be extra work and could sync). The newer TensorDescriptor path has no such buffer.
print(triton.__version__) and the API choice must stay in prepare() only, never inside kernel_fn.

companions.change: From branch hyp/muse_bf16_proj/pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore (the parent this hypothesis builds on), change exactly one constant: POOLER_BLOCK_K from 128 to 256. Keep the plain per-thread tl.load (cp.async) weight path with direct transposed [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] addressing; no TMA descriptor. Keep num_stages=4, num_warps=4, BLOCK_N=64, SPLIT_K=2, grid (64, 2), BLOCK_M=16 for m<=16 and 32 for 17..32. Keep the fp32 workspace, barrier + acq_rel ticket + barrier + fixed-order last-CTA reduce + atomic_xchg reset, routing (pooler m<=32 only), warm-up of m=1..32 and the counter re-zero in prepare(). If 192 KB of smem at BLOCK_M=32 is rejected, use num_stages=3 for that specialization only. The TMA run should then make the same fallback so the arms stay matched. This is byte-for-byte the held pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore-control-blockk256: re-queue that file (clear its hold) instead of minting a new one.

expected.why: 128 KB in flight per CTA, the unpooler config measured at 18.0 us (3.73 TB/s) on the same 67.1 MB; expect ~18-18.5 us kernel vs the parent's 19.5
unpooler BLOCK_M=32 at this tile was 19.8 us kernel vs the parent's 22.7; roughly flat vs cuBLAS's 22.0 shape time

companions.reason: Separates TMA from the bundled BLOCK_K 128->256 change, compared per row on kernel us. If TMA is about 17.5 us and the control about 18.3 us, TMA earns about 0.8 us, and porting it to qkv_gate and unpooler is justified. If both are about 18 us, the gain is all BLOCK_K; drop TMA and promote the simpler cp.async kernel. If the control is faster than TMA, TMA's operand path (mma.sync from TMA-swizzled smem plus trans) costs more than it saves. If both stay about 20 us, the per-CTA geometry is not portable from the unpooler, and the split-K/semaphore design is the limit.

open_questions: Which Triton version does the judge image run? If neither API exists, the hypothesis records that and makes no run. The control is still worth running on its own, because it answers the BLOCK_K question.

Box inner extent: 256 bf16 is 512 B, beyond the 128 B swizzle span. Newer Triton splits such a box into several TMA messages per stage. The old experimental create_2d_tma_descriptor path may reject it or fall back to a non-swizzled layout, which causes bank-conflicted ldmatrix. If so, use a [64,64] box with four loads per K-step, or record the fallback.

At BLOCK_M=16 with 4 warps, Triton lowers tl.dot to mma.sync (MMAv2), not wgmma. Confirm that tl.trans(w) on the TMA NVMMA-shared tile becomes an ldmatrix(.trans) view and not a convert_layout through registers. Print n_regs/n_spills and grep 'cp.async.bulk.tensor' and 'ldmatrix' in kernel.asm['ptx'] in prepare(), since this node cannot compile.

Does Triton's pipeliner keep 4 TMA stages in flight while x is still a masked cp.async load in the same loop? Mixed async groups sometimes collapse the pipeline depth. The PTX mbarrier count, printed in prepare(), answers this.

nvjet already uses TMA and reaches only 3.67 TB/s on this weight. If the TMA arm lands at 18 us rather than 17.5, the per-SM or HBM efficiency ceiling, not the copy mechanism, may be the limit for one 128-CTA wave plus the reduce tail.
